:J U D G M E N T:

This is a claim petition U/Sec.166 of MV Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries suffered by the petitioner in the Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 27.11.2021.
2.

The averments of the petition in brief is as follows:
On 27.11.2021 at about 2.45 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding as an inmate of the Innova Car bearing No. KA.04.MD.4245 towards Dharmastala and when the said car reached near Tippuru cross, on Bangalore - Mangalore road, the towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 was proceeding and in front of that the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 was also proceeding.

At that time, the driver of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 suddenly stopped the vehicle at the middle of the road without giving any indications, due to which the driver of towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 dashed against the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 from behind and the Car in which the petitioner was proceeding was also dashed to the towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 from back side and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to A C Giri hospital, after first aid he was shifted to Sparsh hospital, Bangalore, wherein petitioner took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.
The petitioner has spent Rs.5,00,000/- for over all expenses in toto.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was very healthy doing transportation work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he was unable to do any work as he was doing prior to the accident and lost his earning capacity.
The accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 by its driver.
In this regard the Amruthur Police have registered the case in Cr. No.150/2021 for the offence punishable under Sec.279 & 337 of IPC against the driver of above said vehicle.
The 1st respondent being the owner and the 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence, this petition.
3. In spite of service of notice, 1st respondent has not appeared before the tribunal, hence placed as Exparte.

After service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written Manjunatha K vs R. Bhagyalakshmi on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12046213/
2 statement.
4.

The written statement averments of the 2 nd respondent are hereunder:
This respondent has denied the issuance of policy in respect of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 and the liability of this respondent if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Inter- alia contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle has entrusted the vehicle to the person who was not having valid driving license as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further contended that, the complaint was lodged after the lapse of 4 days from the date of occurrence of accident and the offending Goods Vehicle was falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, the owner and insurer of Innova Car bearing No. KA.04.MD.4245 and towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 were not made as parties to the proceedings.
Hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties to the proceedings.
Further contended that there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
Further it has also denied the age, avocation, income of the petitioner and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, the offending Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 was not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition it.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following:
:ISSUES:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 27.11.2021 at about 2.45 a.m. when he was travelling towards Dharmasthala from Bangalore side near Tippuru cross on Bangalore - Mangalore road, he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Tata 407 Goods Vehicle bearing No.
AP.39.W.8865 by its driver as stated in the petition ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?

If so, to what extent and from whom ?

Perused the records placed before the Tribunal.

The findings of this Tribunal to the above referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.

Issue No.3 :- As per the final order for the following:

:REASONS:
8. ISSUE No.1:- Before going to discuss the issue no.1, it is worth to refer the decision reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that, "it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Therefore, it is crystal clear that the petitioner has to prove his case on the principle of preponderance of probabilities.
9. In order to prove the case of petitioner, he examined himself as P.W.1 by way of filing affidavit in support of his oral examination-in-chief.
Hence, this Tribunal need not to recapitulate the same once again at this juncture.
In order to prove issue No.1, P.W.1 has relied on Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
Accordingly, Ex.P.1 is the true copy of complaint.
Ex.P.2 is the true copy FIR pertaining to Cr.No.150/2021.

Ex.P.7 is the true copy of wound certificate and Ex.P8 is the true copy of charge sheet.
10. In order to substantiate the contention of respondents, the official of 2nd respondent insurance company is examined as RW.1.
R.W.1 has filed affidavit by way of examination-in-chief and produced Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
It is relevant to note that, to substantiate their contention with regard to rash or negligence of offending vehicle, respondent No.2 has not placed positive evidence.

11. The first main contention of the 2nd respondent is that, the complaint was lodged after the lapse of 4 days from the date of occurrence of accident and the offending Goods Vehicle was falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
In the instant case, the petitioner has produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.1, complaint was lodged before Amrutur Police Station on 30.11.2021.

Thereafter, as per Ex.P.2, FIR was lodged against the driver of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No.
AP.39.W.8865.

Further, on careful perusal of Ex.P.7 it appears to this Tribunal that, on 27.11.2021 itself the petitioner took treatment at Adichunchanagiri hospital & Research Center with history of RTA between Car and Tanker.

12. Now, at this juncture, it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court decided in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., reported in 2018 (5) SCC 656 as held that, "Where there is a delay in lodging FIR or registering the case, the tribunal must examine whether the delay has been properly Manjunatha K vs R. 4 explained and whether the explanation is plausible''.

sentences.text: Now the question before this tribunal is whether the petitioner has explained the reasons or not?.
Now it is appropriate to see Ex.P.2.
A careful reading of Ex.P.2, it appears to this Tribunal that, one Sri Umesh G has lodged the complaint.
Further, he has stated that after providing treatment to the petitioner he has lodged the complaint.
Further, charge sheet has been filed by the investigating officer against the driver of the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865.

That apart, as per Ex.P7 wound certificate, the accident took place on 27.11.2021 and the petitioner admitted to the Adhichunchanagiri hospital and research center on that day itself and has sustained grievous injuries.
Further on perusal of Ex.P9 discharge summary, it appears to this tribunal that petitioner took treatment as in inpatient at Sparsh hospital from 27.11.2021 to 01.12.2021.
It is relevant to note that on 30.11.2021 one Sri Umesh G has lodged the complaint.
Therefore, it appears to this Tribunal that, there is no malafide intention in lodging complaint after 4 days of the accident and the reasons assigned for delayed complaint is probable.

At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kusuma Latha Vs. Satbir reported in 2011 (3) SCC 646, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, "the motor vehicles act is a beneficial legislation and that the claims under it must be decided on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities, not proof beyond reasonable doubt''.

13. Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in 2011 (4) SCC 693, between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana and Others, wherein it is held that:
"It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot except a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim".

Further the Hon'ble Apex Court held that: "In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with the closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
The principles reiterated in the above decisions referred to above are squarely applicable to the facts of the case.
Accordingly, there is no merits in the contention raised by respondent No.2 with regard to delay in lodging complaint.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2015 (9)
SCC 273 between Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that:
 (i) In the case of composite  negligence, plaintiff/claimant is  entitled to sue both or any one of the joint tortfeasors and to recover the entire compensation as liability of joint tortfeasors is joint and several.

entities.text: Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ( ii) In the case of composite negligence, apportionment of compensation between two tortfeasors vis a vis the plaintiff/claimant is not permissible.
He can recover at his option whole damages from any of them.
(iii) In case all the joint tortfeasors have been impleaded and evidence is sufficient, it is open to the court/tribunal to determine inter se extent of composite negligence of the drivers.

However,
determination of the extent of negligence between the joint tortfeasors is only for the purpose of their inter se liability so that one may recover the sum from the other after making whole of payment to the plaintiff/claimant to the extent it has satisfied the liability of the other.

In case both of them have been impleaded and the apportionment/ extent of their negligence has been determined by the court/tribunal, in main case one joint tortfeasor can recover the amount from the other in the execution proceedings.
(iv) It would not be appropriate for the court/tribunal to determine the extent of composite negligence of the drivers of two vehicles in the absence of impleadment of other joint tortfeasors.
In such a case, impleaded joint tortfeasor should be left, in case he so desires, to sue the other joint tortfeasor in independent proceedings after passing of the decree or award.
In view of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court the petition against the 2nd respondent is maintainable.

16. Further, on careful perusal of Ex.P.1 & Ex.P.2, it appears to this Tribunal that, on the basis of complaint, the police have registered the case against the driver of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865.
Thereafter the police have conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3.

Further on perusal of Ex.P7 IMV report, it is observed that the offending Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No.
AP.39.W.8865 has got damaged in its rare side and another two vehicles ie., Innova Car bearing No.
KA.04.MD.4245 and towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 were got damaged in their front portion.

Therefore, from Ex.P3 & Ex.P6 it appears to this tribunal that the driver of Tata 407 Goods Manjunatha K vs R. Bhagyalakshmi on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12046213/
6 vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 has suddenly stopped the vehicle without giving any indications and as such the towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 dashed against the said goods vehicle and Innova Car bearing No. KA.04.MD.4245 dashed against the towing vehicle and hence it is clear that the negligence is on the driver of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 in causing the accident.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the investigating officer after completing investigation has filed the charge sheet against the driver of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 as per Ex.P8 for the offences punishable U/Sec. 279, 337 & 338 of IPC and also U/Sec. 190, 192(A), 196 & 177 of MV Act.
Further on careful perusal of Ex.P.7, it clearly goes to show that, the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

17. Now, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reported in ILR 2003 Karnataka page 493, between Mallamma Vs. Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder: " Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
18.

At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that when the petitioner was proceeding as an inmate of the Innova Car bearing No. KA.04.MD.4245, at that time the driver of Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 suddenly stopped the vehicle at the middle of the road without giving any indications, due to which the driver of towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 dashed against the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 from behind and the Car in which the petitioner was proceeding was also dashed to the towing vehicle bearing No. KA.04.C.2800 from back side.
The evidence placed on record clearly reveals that the driver of the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 is the causa causan for the accident.
Hence the contention of respondent No.2 regarding the offending vehicle has not been involved in the accident is not acceptable.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
19. ISSUE No.2:-
This issue is with respect to entitlement of relief.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, accident was occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865 by its driver.
The 1st respondent is the owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
Before going to discuss other aspects, it is appropriate to discuss the age and income of the petitioner.
According to the petitioner, he was aged about 35 years as on the date of accident.
In order to substantiate the same, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.14, the notarized copy of his Aadhaar card which discloses that, the date of birth of the petitioner as 24.07.1987.
The accident was occurred on 27.11.2021.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 34 years and 4 months.

Therefore, by relying on the judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 5353/2024 (MV-D) decided on 07th August 2025 between The Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub BMTC, Shanthinagar, Bengaluru Vs. Smt. Jyothi and others, this tribunal considered the completed age of petitioner.
Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 34 years as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: Income:- According to the petitioner, he was doing transportation business and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Per-contra, the 2 nd respondent has denied the income of petitioner.
To substantiate his income the petitioner has not placed any documentary evidence.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in a case of Godabai and others Vs. Goudappa and another reported in 2024 SCC Online KAR 15570 (Decided in MFA No. 201022/2018 ( MV-D) on 04.06.2024) wherein the Hon'ble Division Bench of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that at para 18 is as here under: "In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority''.

entities.text: Godabai and others Vs. Goudappa and another reported in 2024 SCC Online KAR 15570
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
That apart, the Hon'ble High Court in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I)
on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

22. In the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the petitioner is to be considered by relying on the judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2021 is Rs.15,000/- per month.
In the instant case the accident occurred on 27.11.2021.
Hence the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.

23. Loss of Future Income due to disability:-
According to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
In order to substantiate the same, he has relied on Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.9.
Ex.7 is the wound certificate and Ex.P9 is the discharge summary.
It is relevant to mention that,
respondent

No.2 has disputed the injuries caused to P.W.1.
24.

In order to prove the physical disability/injuries, the petitioner examined medical witness namely Dr. B Ramesh B, Orthopaedic surgeon at Victoria hospital as P.W.2 and produced Ex.P.15,
the OPD book and Ex.P.16 X-rays.
This witness has filed the affidavit in lieu of oral evidence.
In his affidavit he has stated that, the petitioner has sustained left proximal humerus fracture.
Further deposed that, the petitioner underwent treatment in the form internal fixation of humerus.

Further deposed that, the petitioner came for disability assessment on 22.04.2025 and found that, petitioner complains of restriction of joint movements of left shoulder, difficulty to ablution lift weight over the head with left upper limb and combing putting on clothes.
Finally he has assessed the permanent physical disability of left upper limb at 35% and 12% to the whole body.
He was cross-examined from the side of 2nd respondent at length.
During the course of cross-examination, he has admitted that, he is not a treated doctor and only assessed the disability.
Further deposed that, the petitioner has sustained only one simple fracture and it is united.

Further he has deposed that, he has assessed Manjunatha K vs R. Bhagyalakshmi on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12046213/
8
only physical disability to the petitioner and not functional disability.
25. On perusal of the discharge summary of petitioner and evidence of medical witness coupled with wound certificate clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained left proximal humerus fracture.
As such, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and physical deformity.
According to the petitioner, he was doing transportation business.
He has not produced any documents to substantiate his avocation.
Moreover, PW.2 has assessed the physical disability and not the functional disability.
Moreover as per the admission of PW.2, it is manifest that fractures are united.
However, considering the avocation of petitioner and injury, the disability assessed by the P.W.2 is on higher side.
Hence, this Tribunal is considered the functional disability of the petitioner/injured as 5% to the whole body.
26. As discussed supra, age of the injured is considered as 34 years and his income is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month.
Annual income comes to Rs.1,80,000/- (15,000 x 12).
Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of injured as per Sarala Verma case is 16.
If we multiplied yearly income with proper multiplier (1,80,000 X 16), then it comes to Rs.28,80,000/-.
Already this Tribunal has considered the disability of petitioner as 5% to the whole body.
The said amount of Rs.1,44,000/- is awarded to the Injured/Petitioner under the head of loss of Future Income due to disability.
27. Medical Expenses:-
According to the petitioner, he has incurred some amount towards treatment, conveyance and nourishment expenses.
In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.12 for Rs.1,80,492/- supported with medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P11.
This Tribunal has carefully perused the medical bills.
Apart from that, there is no evidence from the side of respondents to disbelieve the medical bills.
After careful perusal of the medical bills, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,80,492/- towards medical expenses.
28. Pain and suffering:-
According to the petitioner, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Sparsh hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient for the injuries sustained by him.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has undergone surgery.
The petitioner has sustained pain because of said injuries and surgery.
Apart from that, as per the evidence of doctor, it appears to this tribunal that, the petitioner has sustained physical deformity.
Moreover the petitioner has sustained one fracture.
As per Ex.P.9 the petitioner was admitted to Sparsh hospital on 27.11.2021 and discharged on 01.12.2021 and also underwent ORIF with PHILOS plate and screws.
Hence, the petitioner has suffered a lot of pain and inconvenience due to accidental injuries.
Therefore, by considering all these aspects, the Tribunal grants compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

29. Loss of income during the laid up period:-
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury and also underwent surgery.

Naturally it shows that, he might have taken at least two Manjunatha K vs R. Bhagyalakshmi on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12046213/
9 months rest because of the injuries.
He has averred that, he was doing transportation business and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But he has not produced documents to substantiate the same.
Hence, this Tribunal has already assessed the income of petitioner as Rs.15,000/- per month.
As per Ex.P.9 the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for a period of 5 days.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laid-up period.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- as compensation under the head of loss of income during laid up period.
30. Food, Nourishment and Attendant charges:-
In so for as food, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges are concerned, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for about 5 days.

Hence,
looking to the injuries sustained and the period of treatment taken by the petitioner,
he is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,500/- under the head of Food, Nourishment and Attendant charges.
31. Loss of future amenities and happiness:-
The petitioner was aged about 34 years at the time of accident.
Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
But the PW.2 doctor has adduced in his evidence that, the fracture is simple in nature and it is united.
Therefore, petitioner has to live with the said deformity for the rest of his life.
Therefore, he might have suffered discomforts in life and loss of amenities.

By considering the age, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability, Rs.15,000/- is awarded under this head.
32. Future medical expenses:- The PW.2 doctor has stated that, petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants.

Hence, by considering the future treatment and evidence of P.W.2,
the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses.

Insurance Policy:- Respondent No.2- the insurance company has denied the issuance of insurance policy with respect to Tata 407 Goods vehicle bearing No. AP.39.W.8865.

Therefore, it is a case of composite negligence.
In a case of composite negligence the liability is always joint and several.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2015 (9) SCC 273 between Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that:
 (i) In the case of composite  negligence, plaintiff/claimant is  entitled to sue both or any one of the joint tortfeasors and to recover the entire compensation as liability of joint tortfeasors is joint and several.
(ii) In the case of composite negligence, apportionment of compensation between two tortfeasors vis a vis the plaintiff/claimant is not permissible.

determination of the extent of negligence between the joint tortfeasors is only for the purpose of their inter se liability so that one may recover the sum from the other after making whole of payment to the plaintiff/claimant to the extent it has satisfied the liability of the other.

In case both of them have been impleaded and the apportionment/ extent of their negligence has been determined by the court/tribunal, in main case one joint tortfeasor can recover the amount from the other in the execution proceedings.

Hence the contention of respondent No.2 regarding the offending vehicle has not been involved in the accident is not acceptable.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
The accident was occurred on 27.11.2021.
Hence, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 34 years and 4 months.
Hence, two months is to be considered as loss of income during laid-up period.
